items.title: Why Mortgage Rates Are Near a One-Year High
items.author: Colin Robertson
items.content: While they aren’t at their absolute worst, mortgage rates remain very close to their one-year high. They’re about .125% below their 52-week highs, which were seen in late July before we got some favorable economic data. However, they remain stubbornly high with no real relief in sight. items.title: Is AI Pushing Mortgage Rates Higher?
items.author: Colin Robertson
items.content: A lot of the recent uptick in mortgage rates has been attributed to the ongoing war with Iran. But there is perhaps another, lesser known reason mortgage rates have pushed back into the high 6s. And it’s all the artificial intelligence (AI) spending, which has arguably crowded out other investments, leading to higher bond yields.… Read More »

items.title: Mortgage Rates Simply Trying to Limit the Damage Right Now
items.author: Colin Robertson
items.content: The best way to sum up mortgage rates right now is any “good news” is simply stopping the bleeding. You’re not seeing sizable drops when positive stuff happens. And we’ve had a few decent things happen lately. All you’re really seeing is rates managing not to get much worse than they already are. And perhaps… Read More »

items.title: Mortgage Rates Get Help From Unexpected Treasury Buyback Program
items.author: Colin Robertson
items.content: Just as it appeared there was no relief in sight for mortgage rates, the Treasury Department stepped in. items.author: Colin Robertson
items.content: The July jobs report just came out and it was very ugly. So ugly that the number of jobs created was negative instead of positive. items.title: Mortgage Rates Move Higher on Jobs Report Defense
items.author: Colin Robertson
items.content: Mortgage rates moved higher again today on the eve of the July jobs report. The monthly jobs report from the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) is always the biggest potential mover of mortgage rates.
